chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Baghdadi al-Varraq narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Ahmad ibn Anbasat, the servant of al-Rashid, narrated that Darim ibn Qabaysa and Naim ibn Salih al-Tabari narrated that Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa, from his father Ja'far, from his father Muhammad, from his father Ali, from his father al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
O God, bless my nation in their early hours on their Saturday and Thursday.

key_terms.يَوْمَ سَبْتِهَا: her Saturday (referring to the nation's Saturday)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Saturday and Thursday mornings in Islamic tradition according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the renowned chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual potency of Thursday and Friday mornings, a practice deeply rooted in Shia devotional culture as times for increased supplication and divine grace. It underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition within the Imams, linking the early hours of these days to specific blessings for the Ummah.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-98 Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Baghdady al-Var’raq narrated that Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Anbasat - the servant of Ar-Rashid quoted Darim ibn Qabaysat narrated that Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (MGB), on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim (MGB), on the authority of his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB) that he had heard his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) say, “God’s Prophet (MGB) prayed and said, ‘O God! Please bless Saturday mornings and Thursday mornings for my nation.”
